question.worked_solution:
We can use either of the following two methods.

**Method 1 - The Long Way**

First, remember that a fraction represents a division:

$$
\frac{(-\frac{7}{4})}{(-9)}=(-\frac{7}{4})÷(-9)
$$

Now, recall that dividing by $-9$ is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal $-\frac{1}{9}.$ We can use this fact to simplify the fraction above: 

$$
\begin{aligned}(-\frac{7}{4})÷(-9) & = \\ (-\frac{7}{4})\times (-\frac{1}{9}) & = \\ \frac{7\times 1}{4\times 9} & = \\ \frac{7}{36}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{(-\frac{7}{4})}{(-9)}=\frac{7}{36}.
$$

**Method 2 - The Quick Way**
The result will have the same numerator as the top fraction, and the denominator is just the product of the two denominators:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(-\frac{7}{4})}{(-9)} & = \\ \frac{-7}{4\times (-9)} & = \\ \frac{-7}{-36} & = \\ \frac{7}{36} & \end{aligned}
$$
